prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map orders the indoor lounge from the bright foreground (~0.3–0.8 m), where the camera wearer's own legs, a grey backpack, and a masked person with a head-mounted camera seated immediately to the left are within arm's reach, to the mid-ground glass coffee table (~1.8–2.5 m ahead on the right) and the dark background couch (~3.5–4.5 m ahead on the left) where two seated people sit side by side about 0.5 m apart. In the foreground, the adjacent left person's head (~0.3–0.5 m in frames 1 and 5) is closer and higher than the backpack resting on the lap (~0.5–0.7 m) and the wearer's knees (~0.6–0.9 m), while the coffee table with a small plant and magazine sits on a white rug below eye level between the foreground seating and the far wall (~5 m). Across frames 1 to 4, the camera wearer turns their head to the right, causing the adjacent person on the left to move gradually out of the left frame edge until only their legs and backpack remain visible in frame 4 while bringing a right-side window (~4–5 m) and the edge of a person or book at the bottom-right corner (~0.5 m) into view, before panning back left in frame 5 as the adjacent person leans closer (~0.3 m). The depth map makes the continuous ground-plane recession and the exact depth layering between the overlapping foreground arms, backpack, and knees much clearer than the RGB image alone. However, it is unreliable on the transparent glass tabletop (which blends with the rug beneath it), saturates to flat white on the closest face in frames 1 and 5, and loses detail in the dark far corner behind the couch.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies discrete scene elements including the tall potted plant on the far left (~4 m), the background couch (~3.5–4 m) with two seated people beside each other (one in cyan on the left, one in grey on the right), and the foreground person and objects within 0.3–1.0 m of the camera wearer. The two background people face roughly toward the foreground and center of the room from ~3.5–4 m away (out of reach of the wearer but within reach of each other), while the foreground person on the left faces forward-right toward the backpack in their lap rather than looking at the camera wearer. As the camera pans right from frame 1 to frame 4 and back left in frame 5, the foreground masks shift horizontally as the left person's head exits and re-enters the left border, and a small mask labeled 'book' briefly appears at the right mid-ground (~2 m, corresponding to the magazines on the glass table) in frame 4. Compared to RGB, the segmentation map sharply delineates the boundaries of the distant seated figures and the tall background plant against the dim wall, and separates overlapping foreground regions in frames 3 and 4. However, it is unreliable in class labeling and mask stability: it misses the glass coffee table and rug entirely, merges the foreground person, backpack, and the wearer's legs into single or fragmented 'person' masks, mislabels small hand/lap regions as 'remote' in frames 2–5, and hallucinate-splits the right-hand couch sitter into duplicate 'person' labels in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty, detecting only foreground hand skeletons (magenta) within arm's reach (~0.4–0.6 m in front of and below the camera wearer) in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, and a single upper-body skeleton (yellow) in frame 4 for the distant person in grey seated on the right end of the couch (~4 m away). In frames 1–3, the magenta keypoints trace the foreground person's hands reaching onto the top of the grey backpack (~0.5 m away, just left of center), shifting from a single detected left hand in frames 1–2 to both hands spaced ~0.15 m apart in frame 3, and then in frame 5 detecting the right hand resting near the person's chest/shoulder (~0.4 m away) as they lean forward. In frame 4, when the camera pans right, the yellow torso-and-leg skeleton shows the right-side couch sitter facing forward and slightly left toward the room center with their torso upright and knees bent downward. Where present, the map isolates exact finger articulation on the backpack and the seated joint geometry of the distant person that are visually cluttered in the RGB strip. However, the map is highly unreliable overall, completely missing the adjacent foreground person's body in all frames, missing the cyan-shirted couch sitter in all five frames, and failing to detect the grey-shirted couch sitter in four of the five frames.
